title: How I Learn by Doing: A Repeatable Mini Project Loop

cover.alt: A fingertip tests a tiny page model connected across a repaired bridge to a public model and a blank lesson notebook.

figures.title: Three artifacts make learning inspectable
figures.summary: The article treats a working result and a record of the process as complementary.

items.label: Local project
items.detail: A small file or repository that can run on your own machine.

items.label: Public deployment
items.detail: A URL where the intended behavior can be tried outside that machine.

items.label: Lesson note
items.detail: A short record of what broke, the fix and the next check to remember.

figures.caption: The three outputs of the mini-project loop. Each contributes different evidence.

figures.title: Finish one small loop
figures.summary: Move a deliberately small example through each real environment.

items.label: Build
items.detail: Create the smallest demo that exercises the idea.

items.label: Verify locally
items.detail: Reload and repeat the intended interaction.

items.label: Save the source
items.detail: Put the working files under version control.

items.label: Deploy and check
items.detail: Publish the artifact, inspect the run and try the live behavior.

items.label: Record
items.detail: Write down the failure, the change and what to check next time.

figures.caption: The article's repeatable process. A runtime timestamp alone does not identify which source revision is deployed.
